accessToken.description: Agent access token: `Authorization: Bearer oneshot_<64 hex>`. A revocable, credits-only credential for agents that run where the wallet key cannot be (hosted MCP clients, cloud runners). Minted by the wallet holder via POST /v1/agents/me/access-tokens. Identifies the agent on every /v1 route in place of X-Agent-ID + x-agent-proof; paid calls are billed to the agent's credit balance (402 `insufficient_credits` when it cannot cover the price) and count against the stored daily budget. Cannot change budgets or mint other tokens.

agentProof.description: Base64 JSON `{ agent, scope, issuedAt, nonce, signature }` where `signature` is an EIP-712 signature (domain `{ name: "OneShot Agent Auth", version: "1" }`, type `AgentReadAuth { agent: address, scope: string, issuedAt: uint256, nonce: bytes32 }`) by the `X-Agent-ID` wallet. `scope` is `read` for reads and `write` for mutations. Proves wallet ownership — the address alone is public. Single-use nonce, 5-minute freshness. The SDKs sign this automatically (TypeScript ≥ 0.25.0, Python ≥ 0.17.0; compute goal routes need TypeScript ≥ 0.44.0, Python ≥ 0.34.0). Required: a request without a valid proof (or an access token) is rejected with 401 `proof_required`. See https://docs.oneshotagent.com/sdk/overview#read-authentication
agentProof.name: x-agent-proof

soulKey.description: Soul seller API key. Format: `Authorization: Bearer soul_<key>`. Obtained via POST /v1/soul/register.

x402Payment.description: x402 payment proof. Send `Authorization: <signed payment header>` and `X-Quote-ID: <quote_id>` after first calling the endpoint to receive a 402 quote. See https://x402.io for the protocol spec.
x402Payment.name: Authorization

info.description:
Tools, payments, and compute orchestration for autonomous AI agents.

## Authentication

- **`x402Payment`** — paid tool endpoints use the [x402 payment protocol](https://x402.io).
  First call returns `402 Payment Required` with a quote; sign and resend the request
  with `Authorization: <signed payment header>` and `X-Quote-ID: <quote_id>`.
- **`agentId`** — free read-only endpoints accept `X-Agent-ID: <wallet>` (0x… address).
- **`soulKey`** — soul marketplace seller dashboard uses `Authorization: Bearer soul_…`
  (issued by `POST /v1/soul/register`).
- **`acpBearer`** — Stripe ACP checkout sessions use a separate bearer token plus the
  `API-Version: 2026-01-30` header.

## Async tools & polling

Most tool endpoints return `202 Accepted` with `{ request_id, tool, status }`. Poll
`GET /v1/requests/{id}` (with the same `X-Agent-ID`) to retrieve the final result.
A WebSocket fallback is available at `wss://<host>/v1/requests/subscribe`.

## Pricing

See [docs.oneshotagent.com/pricing](https://docs.oneshotagent.com/pricing) for the full
table. Per-call costs for this environment, rendered from the same config the routes bill from:

| Tool | Cost |
|---|---|
| Web search | $0.001 |
| Web read | $0.002 |
| Research | $0.01 |
| Person enrichment | $0.005 |
| Email verification | $0.001 |
| Deep research (person) | $0.05 |
| Social profiles | $0.50 |
| Local business search | $0.01 |
| Commerce search | $0.002 |
| LinkedIn history sync | $0.02 per bounded run |
| LinkedIn reply | $0.02 per message |
| LinkedIn profile view | $0.01 per view |
| LinkedIn post reaction | $0.01 per reaction |
| Email send | quote-based; service fee from $0.005 per send |
| SMS send | $0.0035 per segment per recipient |
| Voice call | $0.35/minute + $5.00 number registration on the first call |
| Browser task | quote-based; minimum $0.005 |
| Website build | quote-based; from $1.00 |
| Compute goal | quote-based; minimum budget $1.00 + 20% platform fee |

## Error format

`{ "error": "<machine_code>", "message": "<human readable>", "details": <optional> }`.
Validation errors include a `details` field with the failing field paths.

A held call is not run or charged; retry it with `X-Approval-Id` once approved and it runs once. A matching deny beats a matching require_approval. Refused for agent access-token sessions.

get.description: Returns the agent's configured spend budget plus live utilization for the current UTC day. Agents with no budget row are unlimited: `daily_usdc` is null and `spent_today_usdc` is still reported. Readable with an agent access token; for token sessions `spent_today_usdc` includes credit-funded calls, since credits are what they pay with.

put.description: Upserts the agent's spend budget. Fields are tri-state: an absent key leaves the stored value alone, an explicit `null` clears it (for `alert_at`/`pause_at`, resets to the default 0.8 / 1.0), a number sets it — so a partial update never wipes the caps it didn't mention. Enforced server-side against the receipt ledger on every paid call; over-budget calls receive 403 `budget_exceeded`. The SDKs send this once automatically when constructed with a `budgets` config. Refused with 403 `budgets_read_only_for_access_tokens` for agent access-token sessions — a delegated credential must not be able to raise its own cap.

Enterprise pilot teams top up an agent's prepaid credit balance with a card, without holding USDC (issue #885, part of #858). Creates a Stripe Checkout Session (mode: payment, USD) with the agent id in metadata, invoice generation enabled, and tax ID + company name collection — Stripe renders the receipt/invoice, OneShot does not. The balance is credited only once Stripe confirms payment via the signed webhook, never at session-creation time: redirect the buyer to the returned `url` and poll GET /v1/tools/balance for the credited amount. A card-funded credit is indistinguishable from an x402-funded one for balance, spend budgets, and credit history — only its ledger `source` metadata differs.

post.description: Wallet sessions only. Call once with { amount } and no payment to receive a 402 whose PAYMENT-REQUIRED header prices exactly that amount; sign the USDC authorization and call again with the payment-signature header. The payment settles on-chain and the same amount is added to the agent's credit balance — the balance access-token (hosted MCP) sessions spend from. Access-token sessions are refused with 503 route_unavailable_for_access_tokens: credits cannot be bought with credits. The settlement transaction hash is the idempotency key. The SDKs wrap both legs: TypeScript agent.topUpCredits(amount), Python client.top_up_credits(amount).

Cost: $0.01 per view in production (see the pricing table). Requires the `view_profile` grant. `notify: false` (default) is a data read that still counts toward LinkedIn's ~100 profile retrievals/day guidance; `notify: true` makes the human appear in the target's "who viewed your profile" and cannot be undone. Result via `GET /v1/requests/{request_id}`: a public-safe `profile` summary (name, headline, location, network distance; never contact info). Viewing twice is idempotent upstream, so a timeout is retried immediately and then fails (`provider_unavailable`) — no ambiguous state. Per-account daily cap default 100 (429 `account_send_limit`).

post.description: Cost: $0.01 per reaction in production (see the pricing table). Requires the `react` grant. `post_id` is the LinkedIn social id (urn:li:activity:… / urn:li:ugcPost:…). Re-sending the same reaction is idempotent upstream, so a timeout is retried immediately and then fails — no ambiguous state. Reactions can be removed by the human on LinkedIn but not through this API. Per-account daily cap default 50 (429 `account_send_limit`).
post.summary: React to a post through the connected account (paid; requires Idempotency-Key)

post.description: Cost: $0.02 per message in production (see the pricing table). Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header: a retry replays the accepted response instead of paying and sending twice, and the durable key on the action request makes a duplicate a 409 even if the cache is unavailable. Before payment the route checks ownership, the `reply` grant, account status, that the conversation is not read-only, content safety, and the per-account daily cap (default 50, shared across every caller of that account; 429 `account_send_limit` with `resets_at`). The worker re-checks the grant under a row lock immediately before sending and enforces randomized spacing by deferring, never sleeping. Outcome via `GET /v1/requests/{request_id}`: `sent` (with `provider_message_id`), `failed` with an error code (`grant_revoked`, `account_disconnected`, `recipient_not_connected`, `content_rejected`, `rate_limited`, `account_send_limit`), or `send_status: ambiguous` while OneShot reconciles a timeout against the upstream chat (up to 24 h; an unconfirmed send is never re-sent blindly and never auto-refunded). A message LinkedIn accepted cannot be recalled.
post.summary: Send a reply in an existing conversation (paid; requires Idempotency-Key)

post.description: Cost: $0.02 per bounded run in production (see the pricing table). One flat price buys up to `max_pages` × 250 messages, newest first, each page committed with its cursor. A run that hits the bound is `paused` with a durable cursor; the next `continue` call resumes it. Empty runs are charged (the enumeration ran); rejections before payment (ownership, grant, status, run already active) are free. Poll `GET /v1/requests/{request_id}` for live progress and `GET /accounts/{id}/sync` for coverage. Never charged for internal reconciliation runs.

post.description: Gets the agent a voice number without placing a call, so it can answer calls (then PUT /v1/tools/voice/numbers/{id}/inbound). Returns the agent's existing active number for free (200); otherwise buys one (201) and charges the one-time phone registration fee from prepaid credits (POST /v1/credits/top-up). The fee is debited before anything is bought: too little credit returns 402 and buys nothing; a failed purchase is refunded. A concurrent request for the same agent returns 409 — retry. Refused for agent access-token sessions.

put.description: Creates or replaces how the number answers inbound calls (a full replace: omitted optional fields take their defaults, and an omitted webhook_url removes the webhook). During business hours the configured assistant answers; after hours it takes a message, transfers, or declines. Calls are paid from prepaid credits (POST /v1/credits/top-up), per started minute at the voice call rate; a call is declined when credits cannot cover the minimum call fee, and a call never runs longer than the credits pay for. Refused for agent access-token sessions.
